narrative.overview:
Bramia's world is the studio's own ad turned into a page: a carbon ground, heavy off-white Archivo posters that end in a silver full stop, rows of outlined lettering sliding behind them, and a brushed-metal ribbon looping like the curls of the B. Everything is black, graphite and silver; light is the only accent. The page reads as a sequence of posters separated by a silver thread, with working demonstrations (a phone lock screen receiving notifications, a search result list, an automation chain) set between them as physical objects.

Density is low and the scale contrast is extreme: posters run up to 124px with 0.86 leading, while body copy sits at 16 to 18px Manrope in stone grey. Motion is part of the material, not decoration: letters rise out of masks, outline rows slide on long linear loops, outlined titles fill solid on scroll, and the B mark reveals the wordmark with a light sweep. All motion collapses under reduced-motion preferences.

Absence is drawn too. Ghost lettering stays visible behind the lit headline, a missing search listing is hatched rather than omitted, and outlined numerals turn silver only when reached.
keyCharacteristics: Carbon ground (#1C1C1C), never pure black; silver as the only accent, no hue.
Uppercase Archivo 900 posters, widened (112%), tightly led, each ending in a silver full stop.
Outlined "ghost" lettering (text-stroke, no fill) as a recurring second voice.
Hairline graphite seams separate rows and panels; deep soft shadows belong only to objects (phone, browser, search panel).
Pill-shaped actions with a round dark arrow chip.
A fixed 3D brushed-metal ribbon behind the content, full strength in the opening viewport and dimmed elsewhere.

rules.name: The No-Hue Rule
rules.body: The palette is carbon, graphite, stone and silver. No orange, no brand colour; client screenshots are the only colour on the page.

rules.name: The Silver Full Stop Rule
rules.body: Every poster headline ends with its punctuation in silver. That full stop is the system's signature accent and should not be spent elsewhere on headlines.

rules.name: The Poster Rule
rules.body: Headlines are uppercase Archivo 900, widened, led below 0.9, and they reveal letter by letter from a mask with a slight rotation (900ms ease-out, 22ms stagger). Everything that is not a claim is Manrope in sentence case.

rules.name: The Ghost Letter Rule
rules.body: Outline lettering (text-stroke, transparent fill) is the second voice of the world: sliding rows behind posters, unfilled service titles, unreached step numerals. It is always decorative or a state, never the only carrier of readable content.

rules.name: The Seam Rule
rules.body: Panels are separated by graphite hairlines, not by shadow. A shadow means "this is an object you could hold".

dos: **Do** end every poster headline with a silver full stop and reveal it letter by letter from a mask.
**Do** separate rows and panels with 1px graphite seams; save the deep soft shadow for device and screen objects.
**Do** keep outline lettering decorative or stateful (aria-hidden rows, unfilled titles, unreached numerals).
**Do** label every demonstration with the example label (silver dot, muted stone 12px).
**Do** show real client screenshots inside browser and phone frames; they are the only colour on the page.
**Do** keep the 3D ribbon behind content and dim it outside the opening viewport (about 0.2 on desktop, 0.14 on mobile, 0.45 at the close).
**Do** collapse all animation under prefers-reduced-motion and stop the outline rows.
donts: **Don't** introduce a hue accent; no orange, no brand colour beyond silver.
**Don't** use pure black (#000) as the ground; the world is carbon.
**Don't** place small labels or kickers above poster headlines; the poster opens the section on its own.
**Don't** turn services or steps into boxed cards; they are hairline-divided rows.
**Don't** set body or explanatory copy in Archivo or in uppercase.
